q: Closest to 100. Use each of the digit cards 2, 4, 7 and 9 once to make two two-digit numbers. Add them. What is the closest total to 100 you can make?
s: The tens digits matter most. Tens 2 and 7 give 90; then the ones 4 + 9 = 13, so 24 + 79 = 103. Tens 2 and 4 give only 60 + 16 = 76, and any other pair of tens gives 110 or more. So 103 (3 away) is the closest.

q: The missing score. Ava and Ben scored 86 points between them. Ben and Cara scored 94. Ava and Cara scored 80. What did each friend score?
s: Add all three clues: 86 + 94 + 80 = 260. Each friend is counted twice, so the three scores add to 260 ÷ 2 = 130. Cara = 130 − 86 = 44. Ava = 130 − 94 = 36. Ben = 130 − 80 = 50.

q: The wheel workshop. A mechanic has 18 scooters and go-karts altogether. Each scooter has 2 wheels and each go-kart has 4. There are 50 wheels. How many go-karts are there?
s: If all 18 were scooters there would be 18 × 2 = 36 wheels. There are 50 − 36 = 14 extra wheels. Each go-kart adds 2 extra wheels, so 14 ÷ 2 = 7 go-karts (and 11 scooters). Check: 11 scooters have 22 wheels and 7 go-karts have 28 wheels, and 22 + 28 = 50.
src: Puzzle ideas from the parent; reworded for this app

q:
One tile short. A mosaic is 8 tiles wide and 9 tiles tall. You use the same tiles to make it 1 tile wider and 1 tile shorter.
a) Will you have tiles left over, need extra, or have exactly enough?
b) Now start with a mosaic 7 wide and 9 tall. What happens this time?
a: a) Exactly enough   b) Need 1 extra
s: a) 8 × 9 = 72 and 9 × 8 = 72, so exactly enough. b) 7 × 9 = 63 and 8 × 8 = 64, so you need 1 extra tile. Making it wider adds a column of tiles as tall as the new mosaic; making it shorter takes away a row as wide as the old one. They only balance when those match.
src: Puzzle ideas from the parent; reworded for this app
wrong: a) Need 1 extra   b) Exactly enough
a) 1 left over   b) Need 1 extra
a) Exactly enough   b) 1 left over
hint: Work out how many tiles are in each mosaic: width × height. Compare the two answers.

q: In a class, there were 5 times as many children present as absent. 30 children were present. How many children are in the class altogether?

q:
A farmer has 72 animals. He has 8 times as many sheep as cows.
a) How many cows does he have?
b) How many sheep does he have?
s: Think of the smaller group as 1 part and the bigger group as 8 parts: 9 parts altogether. 72 ÷ 9 = 8, so 1 part = 8. Cows: 8. Sheep: 8 × 8 = 64.
